turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on a, an and the?
turns.tutor:
Hi! First, watch me do one.
She eats ___ apple. "Apple" starts with the sound "a". That is a vowel sound. So I write "an": She eats an apple.
Rule: "an" goes before a vowel sound; "a" goes before other sounds.
Right: I have a pen. Wrong: I have an pen.
Your turn. Write a or an:
She has ___ orange in her bag. (answer with only the missing word)
turns.judgeInput:

Target form: articles. Learner level A1. First language Arabic.
W1 (wrong) strength 1: no a/an is needed before a singular noun. Its error: leaves out a/an ("She is teacher").
W2 (wrong) strength 3: a and an are the same; "a" (or "the") goes everywhere. Its error: uses "a" where "an" is needed ("a apple").
C1 (correct) strength 0: a singular countable noun needs a/an (or the). Independent correct productions so far: 0.
C2 (correct) strength 0: an before a vowel sound, a before a consonant sound. Independent correct productions so far: 0.
